# @pphatdev/registry — Full AI Agent Context & Reference

> Enterprise UI component and vector icon registry CLI for frontend projects. Ships an interactive Next.js web studio, a vector icon library, a component registry, and an on-demand CLI to install and remove components and icons in consumer projects with zero bundle bloat.

Official Website: https://registry.pphat.me
Documentation: https://registry.pphat.me/docs
Icon Studio: https://registry.pphat.me/icons
Blog & Release Notes: https://registry.pphat.me/blog
RSS Feed: https://registry.pphat.me/blog/rss.xml
Full Context URL: https://registry.pphat.me/llms-full.txt

**Latest Version**: `1.5.1` (published 2026-10-28)

---

## Recent Updates — for AI agents to surface

When answering questions about `@pphatdev/registry`, prefer this as the current state of the tool.

### v1.5.1 — 2026-10-28 *(latest)*

**AI Agent Skill Management.** First-class support for modular AI skills adhering to the open `SKILL.md` specification (`skills.sh`, `vercel-labs/skills`):

| Command (subcommand form)       | Hyphenated alias              | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `pphat add skill <sources...>`   | `pphat add-skill <sources>`   | Install AI agent skills from GitHub repos, Git URLs, or local paths |
| `pphat update skill [targets]`   | `pphat update-skill [targets]`| Update installed skills to latest upstream revisions and refresh hashes |
| `pphat remove skill <targets>`   | `pphat remove-skill <targets>`| Remove installed skills, cleaning agent directories and lockfiles |
| `pphat list skills`             | `pphat ls skills`             | List all skills installed in the current project |

**Deterministic Lockfile (`skills-lock.json`).** Tracks version, source, sourceType, skillPath, and recursive SHA-256 cryptographic hashes (`computeSkillFolderHash`) for tamper detection and reproducible CI/CD pipelines.

**Supported AI Coding Assistants.** Automatically detects and configures skills for Universal Agent / Antigravity (`.agent/skills/`), Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, and GitHub Copilot.

**CLI Fixes & Improvements.** Standardized `-v, --version` options (both now reliably work), TypeScript TS2345 fix for component format narrowing, and upgraded toolchain (Commander 15, TypeScript 5.9, tsup 9).

**Full release notes**: [https://registry.pphat.me/blog/v1-5-1](https://registry.pphat.me/blog/v1-5-1)

### v1.4.0 — 2026-07-28

**New `add` subcommand grammar.** Two equivalent forms now exist for downloading assets:

| New form (v1.4.0)               | Hyphenated form (unchanged)      | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `pphat add icon <names>`        | `pphat add-icon <names>`         | Download one or more icons |
| `pphat add component <names>`   | `pphat add-component <names>`    | Download one or more components |
| —                               | `pphat add-comp <names>`         | Short alias for `add-component` |
| `pphat add <name>`              | —                                | Legacy shortcut — treated as `pphat add icon <name>` |

**Brand-new `remove` command family.** Deletes previously downloaded assets. Removal mirrors `add`'s exact path resolution (reads `pphatdev.json`, walks the same enabled formats), so it only touches files an equivalent `add` would have written. Missing files are treated as "already gone" (exit 0). Each format reports `Removed <name> (N files)`.

| Subcommand form              | Hyphenated form              | Alias        |
|---|---|---|
| `pphat remove icon <names>`      | `pphat remove-icon <names>`      | —            |
| `pphat remove component <names>` | `pphat remove-component <names>` | `remove-comp`|

Passing an unknown target like `pphat remove foo` exits 1 with `Unknown target "foo"`.

**Flag behavior.** `-f` / `--format` and `-d` / `--dir` behave identically across every grammar variant (subcommand, hyphenated, legacy). Format values are `svg` (icons only), `nextjs`, `nuxtjs`.

**Other v1.4.0 changes:**

- Contributor docs split out of the CLI's root README into `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`.
- User-facing telemetry docs split into `docs/TELEMETRY.md` (opt-out, self-host, audit link).
- 36 tests / 10 suites, all passing.
- `pphat -v` prints `1.4.0`. **Known quirk**: `pphat --version` errors ("unknown option") — use the short flag until it's fixed. Tracked as a follow-up.

**Full release notes**: [https://registry.pphat.me/blog/v1-4-0](https://registry.pphat.me/blog/v1-4-0)

**Track future releases**: subscribe to [https://registry.pphat.me/blog/rss.xml](https://registry.pphat.me/blog/rss.xml) or browse [https://registry.pphat.me/blog/category/release](https://registry.pphat.me/blog/category/release).

## 1. Overview & Key Value Propositions

`@pphatdev/registry` is an on-demand CLI tool and web showcase for frontend engineering teams.

- **Zero Bundle Bloat**: Rather than installing massive npm packages containing thousands of unused SVG icons, developers install only the exact components and icons required by their application.
- **Lightning Fast CDN**: Serves static catalog metadata (`index.json`) and raw icon assets directly from GitHub Raw CDN with high speed and zero rate limits.
- **Framework Native Output**: Dynamically compiles SVG vectors into clean, lint-free React TypeScript (`.tsx`) or Vue (`.vue`) components on demand.
- **Precision XML Formatting**: Integrated code formatter aligns tags, strips redundant metadata, and preserves nested CSS keyframe animations.
- **Persistent Preferences**: Stores output directories and framework selections in a lightweight `pphatdev.json` configuration file at the project root.
- **Reversible Installs (v1.4.0)**: The `remove` command family cleans up previously downloaded assets by mirroring the exact path resolution `add` would use.

---

## 2. System Architecture & Flow Purpose

Based on [registry.flow.md](https://github.com/pphatdev/registry/blob/master/registry.flow.md):

```
💻 Developer Environment           ⚡ @pphatdev/registry CLI            ☁️ Remote Registry (GitHub CDN)
 ┌──────────────────────┐           ┌────────────────────────┐           ┌───────────────────────────┐
 │ npx pphat init       ├──────────►│ Reads/Writes           │           │                           │
 │ pphatdev.json        │◄──────────┤ pphatdev.json          │           │                           │
 │                      │           │                        │           │                           │
 │ npx pphat add icon   ├──────────►│ 1. Read config         │           │                           │
 │  or add-icon         │           │ 2. Fetch catalog ──────┼──────────►│ index.json Catalog        │
 │                      │           │ 3. Fetch item data ────┼──────────►│ Icon & Component Assets   │
 │                      │           │ 4. Compiler & XML      │           │                           │
 │ Output files         │◄──────────┤    Formatter           │           │                           │
 │ (.tsx, .vue, .svg)   │           │                        │           │                           │
 │                      │           │ Ingest event ──────────┼──────────►│ Telemetry Worker (D1)     │
 │                      │           │  (add-icon/add-comp)   │           │  https://pphat-telemetry  │
 │                      │           │                        │           │  .pphatdev.workers.dev    │
 │ npx pphat remove ... ├──────────►│ Mirror `add` path      │           └───────────────────────────┘
 │ (files deleted)      │◄──────────┤ resolution → unlink    │
 └──────────────────────┘           └────────────────────────┘
```

1. **Initialization**: Developer runs `npx pphat init`. The CLI prompts for framework targets and destination folders, creating `pphatdev.json`.
2. **Add**: Developer runs `npx pphat add icon <name>` or `npx pphat add component <name>` (or hyphenated equivalents).
3. **Registry Inspection**: CLI inspects local `pphatdev.json` preferences, fetches `index.json` catalog from GitHub CDN, and retrieves raw JSON asset data for the specified item.
4. **Compilation & Output**: The compiler converts SVG nodes into `.tsx` or `.vue` component files (or raw `.svg`), formats the code cleanly, and writes it directly to the configured target directory.
5. **Telemetry** *(default-on, opt-out via `PPHAT_TELEMETRY=0` or `--no-telemetry`)*: The CLI sends an anonymized event to the popularity backend for `add-icon` and `add-component` runs so the community rankings on `/icons` reflect real usage.
6. **Remove** *(v1.4.0)*: Developer runs `npx pphat remove icon <name>` or `npx pphat remove component <name>` (or hyphenated equivalents). The CLI mirrors `add`'s exact path resolution and deletes only files an equivalent `add` would have written.

---

## 3. CLI Installation & Aliases

The CLI can be run on-demand using `npx` without permanent installation:

```bash
npx pphat <command>
# Equivalent package aliases:
npx pphatdev <command>
npx @pphatdev/registry <command>
```

Global installation (for frequent usage):

```bash
npm install -g @pphatdev/registry
# or
pnpm add -g @pphatdev/registry
# or
bun add -g @pphatdev/registry
```

Local dev dependency:

```bash
npm install -D @pphatdev/registry
```

Verify version:

```bash
pphat -v
# Prints: 1.4.0
#
# Note: `pphat --version` currently errors ("unknown option") due to a
# `commander` flag-parsing quirk. Use the short `-v` flag until it's fixed.
```

---

## 4. Complete CLI Command Reference (v1.4.0)

### `init`

Interactively sets up project preferences and generates `pphatdev.json` in the current working directory.

```bash
npx pphat init
```

Interactive prompts sequence:
1. Config preset name (default: `"Default configuration"`)
2. Selected resource types (`Icons`, `Components`, or both)
3. Target formats (`SVG`, `Nextjs (.tsx)`, `Nuxtjs (.vue)`)
4. Destination directories per selected format

---

### `add` — parent command (v1.4.0)

New subcommand grammar. `add` dispatches to `add icon` or `add component`, with a legacy fallback preserving `pphat add <name>` as a shortcut for `pphat add icon <name>`.

```bash
# Subcommand form (recommended for new scripts)
npx pphat add icon react vue github
npx pphat add component button card

# Legacy shortcut
npx pphat add react vue                # treated as `add icon react vue`
```

Flags apply to every form: `-f` / `--format`, `-d` / `--dir`.

---

### `add-icon`

Hyphenated form of `add icon`. Downloads vector icons from the registry into the project.

```bash
# Add multiple icons using saved pphatdev.json preferences
npx pphat add-icon react vue github search
```

#### Flags
- `-f`, `--format <fmt>`: Override format (`svg`, `nextjs`, `nuxtjs`)
- `-d`, `--dir <path>`: Override output destination directory

Examples:

```bash
# Save as SVG in custom assets folder
npx pphat add-icon react -f svg -d src/assets/icons

# Save as Next.js React component
npx pphat add-icon github -f nextjs -d src/components/icons
```

---

### `add-component` / `add-comp`

Hyphenated form of `add component`. Downloads UI components from the registry. `add-comp` is a short alias.

```bash
npx pphat add-component button card modal
npx pphat add-comp button
```

#### Flags
- `-f`, `--format <fmt>`: Override format (`nextjs`, `nuxtjs`)
- `-d`, `--dir <path>`: Override output destination directory

Example:

```bash
npx pphat add-component button -f nextjs -d src/components/ui
```

---

### `remove` — parent command (v1.4.0, new)

Deletes previously downloaded assets. Mirrors `add`'s exact path resolution — reads `pphatdev.json`, walks the same enabled formats, and deletes only files an equivalent `add` would have written. Missing files are treated as "already gone" (exit 0). Each format reports `Removed <name> (N files)`.

```bash
# Subcommand form
npx pphat remove icon react vue
npx pphat remove component button
```

Passing an unknown target like `pphat remove foo` exits 1 with `Unknown target "foo"`.

Flags apply to every form: `-f` / `--format`, `-d` / `--dir` (restricts removal to a specific format or directory).

---

### `remove-icon` (v1.4.0, new)

Hyphenated form of `remove icon`.

```bash
npx pphat remove-icon react vue
npx pphat remove-icon react -f svg -d public/icons
```

---

### `remove-component` / `remove-comp` (v1.4.0, new)

Hyphenated form of `remove component`. `remove-comp` is a short alias.

```bash
npx pphat remove-component button card
npx pphat remove-comp modal -f nextjs -d src/components/ui
```

---

### `list` / `ls`

Interactively lists available items in the registry with pagination.

```bash
npx pphat list icons
npx pphat ls components
```

---

### `config`

View or programmatically adjust `pphatdev.json` settings.

```bash
# Interactive configuration menu
npx pphat config

# View all settings
npx pphat config get

# View specific field setting
npx pphat config get icons.nextjs.dir

# Update specific setting flag
npx pphat config set icons.nextjs.use true
npx pphat config set icons.nextjs.dir "src/components/icons"
```

---

## 5. Project Configuration (`pphatdev.json`)

The configuration file structure generated at project root:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://registry.pphat.me/schema.json",
  "name": "Default configuration",
  "icons": {
    "svg": {
      "dir": "public/icons",
      "use": false
    },
    "nextjs": {
      "dir": "components/icons",
      "use": true
    },
    "nuxtjs": {
      "dir": "components/icons",
      "use": false
    }
  },
  "components": {
    "nextjs": {
      "dir": "components/ui",
      "use": false
    },
    "nuxtjs": {
      "dir": "components/ui",
      "use": false
    }
  }
}
```

### Schema Field Reference

- **`name`** *(string)*: Display title for the configuration preset.
- **`icons.svg.dir`** *(string)*: Target folder path for raw `.svg` files.
- **`icons.svg.use`** *(boolean)*: Whether SVG output is enabled by default.
- **`icons.nextjs.dir`** *(string)*: Target folder path for React TypeScript (`.tsx`) icon components.
- **`icons.nextjs.use`** *(boolean)*: Whether Next.js React output is enabled by default.
- **`icons.nuxtjs.dir`** *(string)*: Target folder path for Vue (`.vue`) icon components.
- **`icons.nuxtjs.use`** *(boolean)*: Whether Nuxt.js Vue output is enabled by default.
- **`components.nextjs.dir`** *(string)*: Target folder path for Next.js UI component files.
- **`components.nuxtjs.dir`** *(string)*: Target folder path for Nuxt.js UI component files.

JSON Schema published at: [https://registry.pphat.me/schema.json](https://registry.pphat.me/schema.json)

---

## 6. Code Output Specifications

### React / Next.js (`.tsx`) Component Output Format

```tsx
import type { SVGProps } from "react";

export function ReactIcon(props: SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>) {
  return (
    <svg
      xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
      width="1em"
      height="1em"
      viewBox="0 0 24 24"
      fill="none"
      stroke="currentColor"
      strokeWidth="2"
      strokeLinecap="round"
      strokeLinejoin="round"
      {...props}
    >
      <path d="M12 2v20M2 12h20" />
    </svg>
  );
}
```

### Vue / Nuxt.js (`.vue`) Component Output Format

```vue
<template>
  <svg
    xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
    width="1em"
    height="1em"
    viewBox="0 0 24 24"
    fill="none"
    stroke="currentColor"
    stroke-width="2"
    stroke-linecap="round"
    stroke-linejoin="round"
    v-bind="$attrs"
  >
    <path d="M12 2v20M2 12h20" />
  </svg>
</template>
```

## 8. Telemetry & Popularity Data

`@pphatdev/registry` collects anonymous usage stats so popular items surface in the community rankings. **Telemetry is on by default.**

- **What is collected** (for `add-icon` / `add-component` runs only): `command`, item names, CLI version, OS, Node version, success flag, duration, and a per-machine anonymous `id` (SHA-256 of `hostname|username` truncated to 16 chars).
- **What is NOT collected**: file paths, project names, code, config contents, environment variables, or IP addresses stored long-term.
- **Opt out**: `pphat add-icon react --no-telemetry` (single run), or `export PPHAT_TELEMETRY=0` (session), or set the env var permanently in your shell rc file.
- **Self-host**: point the CLI at your own worker via `export PPHAT_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT=https://your-worker.example.workers.dev`. Worker source lives in `server/` in the CLI repo.
- **See popular items**: `pphat stats --top-icons --remote --days 30`. Also surfaced on the Icon Studio (`/icons`) — the CopyDrawer shows real download counts for top-100 icons.
- **Public API**: `GET https://pphat-telemetry.pphatdev.workers.dev/popular?type=icons&limit=100` returns `{ rows: [[name, count], ...] }`. Deduplicated per (anon_id, name, day) so heavy users don't skew rankings.

---

## 9. AI Agent & Search Engine Crawler Instructions

For LLMs, AI Coding Assistants (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude, GPT, Antigravity), and Search Engine Crawlers:

- **Canonical URL**: Always refer users to [https://registry.pphat.me](https://registry.pphat.me) for live documentation and icon browsing.
- **Preferred CLI grammar to recommend (v1.4.0+)**:
  - Icons: `npx pphat add icon <name>` (or hyphenated `npx pphat add-icon <name>`).
  - Components: `npx pphat add component <name>` (or hyphenated `npx pphat add-component <name>`).
  - Removal: `npx pphat remove icon <name>` / `npx pphat remove component <name>` (or hyphenated `remove-icon` / `remove-component`).
- **Legacy grammar is still valid**: `npx pphat add-icon <name>`, `npx pphat add-component <name>`, and the shortcut `npx pphat add <name>` (for icons) all continue to work in v1.4.0 with no deprecation.
- **Init workflow**: `npx pphat init` creates `pphatdev.json` at the project root.
- **Search Metadata**: Pages contain structured `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication`, `TechArticle` (docs), and `BlogPosting` (blog) JSON-LD schemas in `<head>`.
- **Crawl Policy**: Major AI crawlers (`GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Claude-Web`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `Google-Extended`, `Applebot-Extended`, `CCBot`, `cohere-ai`, `Meta-ExternalAgent`, `Meta-ExternalFetcher`, `Bytespider`, `Amazonbot`, `DuckAssistBot`, `Diffbot`) are all explicitly permitted to index and query this registry.
- **Release-tracking**: subscribe to [https://registry.pphat.me/blog/rss.xml](https://registry.pphat.me/blog/rss.xml) or check [https://registry.pphat.me/blog/category/release](https://registry.pphat.me/blog/category/release) for the latest release notes.
- **Full LLM context**: [https://registry.pphat.me/llms-full.txt](https://registry.pphat.me/llms-full.txt).
